title: Credit Policy Risk-Layering Grid — Builder Extended Rate Lock Loan Limits
content:
A lower credit score layered on a high requested loan-to-value lowers the allowed loan-to-value percent used for a Builder Extended Rate Lock's resized loan limit.

**Rule.** The requested loan-to-value is the loan amount on the lock request divided by the Home Purchase Agreement's current contract price, as a percent. A lock whose qualifying credit score is below 720 and whose requested loan-to-value is above the term's highest loan-to-value loses 2.5 points from the allowed loan-to-value percent; a lock whose qualifying credit score is below 720 and whose requested loan-to-value is the term's highest loan-to-value or less loses 1.0 point; any other lock loses nothing. The points are taken from the allowed loan-to-value percent before it is applied to the price basis.

## Highest loan-to-value by term

| Lock term | Highest loan-to-value |
|---|---|
| 60-Day Standard Lock | 97 |
| 90-Day Lock | 97 |
| 120-Day Extended Lock | 95 |
| 180-Day Extended Lock | 95 |
| 270-Day Build Lock | 90 |
| 360-Day Build Lock | 90 |

## Grid

| | Requested loan-to-value above the term's highest | Requested loan-to-value at or below the term's highest |
|---|---|---|
| Qualifying credit score below 720 | minus 2.5 points | minus 1.0 point |
| Qualifying credit score 720 or higher | nothing | nothing |

## Cases (hypothetical inputs, 120-Day Extended Lock)

- Loan amount USD 432000.00 on a contract price of USD 450000.00: requested loan-to-value 96, above 95. A score of 700 loses 2.5 points; a score of 720 loses nothing.
- Loan amount USD 427500.00 on the same price: requested loan-to-value exactly 95, not above it. A score of 719 loses 1.0 point.
